angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,043,550 km at 158.71 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.3006 +/- 0.0198 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 158.71 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.5 +/- 0.03 solar radii from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-330 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract): 1,043,550 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.23 +/- 0.02 solar masses from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-330 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6232 +/- 33 K from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-330 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-330 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-330.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.176, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
